nodes.label: Editor's Introduction to the Ingredient Section
nodes.summary: Editor's introduction to the 9th edition ingredient section. Highlights breakthrough technologies: biotech/fermentation (land to laboratory), plant stem cells, marine ingredients, skin whitening, and hyaluronic acid advances, with a focus on anti-aging needs of an aging population.

nodes.label: Biotechnology/Fermentation Ingredient Production
nodes.summary: 'From land to laboratory': using biotech and fermentation to produce cosmetic ingredients, highlighted as a breakthrough technology.

nodes.label: Plant Stem Cell Technology
nodes.summary: Highlighted as one of the breakthrough ingredient technologies of the last decade.

nodes.label: Marine Ingredients
nodes.summary: Development and utilization of marine-derived ingredients is highlighted as a breakthrough area.

nodes.label: Skin Whitening
nodes.summary: Breakthroughs in skin whitening are highlighted among key ingredient developments.

nodes.label: Hyaluronic Acid
nodes.summary: Advancement in hyaluronic acid is cited as a breakthrough ingredient technology.

nodes.label: Skin Aging
nodes.summary: Preventing aging is described as a major area driven by the escalating senior population.

nodes.label: Surfactants
nodes.summary: Surveys surfactants: history, functions (emulsifying, cleaning, foaming, solubilizing, conditioning, dispersing, lubricating), applications in creams, shampoos, cleansers, conditioners, color cosmetics and antiperspirants, physical chemistry (surface tension, micelles, charge, foam), and chemistry of anionic, nonionic, amphoteric and cationic classes.

nodes.label: Surfactants
nodes.summary: Surface active agents; amphiphilic molecules with hydrophilic polar head and hydrophobic tail that lower interfacial tension. Classified into anionic, nonionic, cationic and amphoteric by charge.

nodes.label: Soap
nodes.summary: The original naturally derived anionic surfactant, used since the Akkadians c. 2800 BCE; made by boiling fats with ashes; soap-stabilized emulsions need pH above 7.

nodes.label: Anionic Surfactants
nodes.summary: Surfactants with net negative charge; used in largest volume for foaming and cleansing and as emulsifiers; skin/eye irritation potential can be high.

nodes.label: Nonionic Surfactants
nodes.summary: Surfactants with no charge, first developed in the 1930s by Atlas Powder Company (sorbitan esters); best solubilizers; used for steric stabilization.

nodes.label: Cationic Surfactants
nodes.summary: Surfactants with net positive charge; attach to negatively charged hair and skin to condition; high irritation potential.

nodes.label: Amphoteric Surfactants
nodes.summary: Zwitterionic surfactants that change charge with pH (cationic at low pH, anionic at alkaline); used to increase mildness in shampoos.

nodes.label: HLB System
nodes.summary: Hydrophile-Lipophile Balance system designed by William C. Griffin; HLB = weight % hydrophilic portion / 5 (e.g. Steareth-20 = 15); composite HLB is arithmetic; oils have required HLB.

nodes.label: Required HLB Test
nodes.summary: Blends of sorbitan oleate (HLB 4.3) and polysorbate 80 (HLB 14.9) at even HLB 6-14 are shaken with test oil and water; least separation gives oil's HLB requirement.

nodes.label: Emulsion
nodes.summary: Kinetically stable but thermodynamically unstable dispersion of oil and water; surfactants aid droplet creation and stabilization against creaming, Ostwald ripening and coalescence.

nodes.label: Emulsion Stabilization
nodes.summary: Four main mechanisms: charge (ionic), steric (nonionic), liquid crystalline lamellar phase, and polymeric stabilization; seldom used in isolation.

nodes.label: Charge Stabilization
nodes.summary: Ionic double layer around droplets creates electrical repulsion; used almost exclusively in O/W emulsions with soaps, phosphate esters or cationics.

nodes.label: Steric Stabilization
nodes.summary: Nonionic emulsifier film around droplets; requires most formulation work but withstands extreme pH, electrolytes and oil polarities.

nodes.label: Liquid Crystalline Lamellar Phase
nodes.summary: Surfactant structures similar to skin lipid bilayers; emulsions resist wash-off, enhance moisturization and delivery of water-soluble actives; independent of HLB.

nodes.label: Polymeric Stabilization
nodes.summary: Polymers stabilize O/W emulsions by building zero-shear viscosity and a polymer matrix between droplets; improve high-temperature stability.

nodes.label: Ostwald Ripening
nodes.summary: An emulsion instability against which droplets must be stabilized.

nodes.label: Micelle
nodes.summary: Spherical surfactant aggregates in water with hydrophobic tails inside; form above the critical micelle concentration; oil dissolves in interior (solubilization).

nodes.label: Critical Micelle Concentration
nodes.summary: Surfactant concentration at which micelles begin to form.

nodes.label: Micellar Solubilization
nodes.summary: IUPAC: incorporation of a solubilizate into or on micelles; nonionics are best solubilizers, e.g. for fragrance in clear shampoos.

nodes.label: Surface Tension Reduction
nodes.summary: Surfactants lower water surface tension at air/water interface, allowing better wetting for cleansing.

nodes.label: Foam
nodes.summary: Dispersion of gas in a small volume of liquid; anionics give highest foam; no physical role in cleansing but a key consumer cue of luxury.

nodes.label: Marangoni Effect
nodes.summary: Mechanism by which foams eventually break when film drainage becomes too great.

nodes.label: Cleansing
nodes.summary: Wetting the substrate, removing soil and suspending it to prevent redeposition; surfactant tails attach to soil, which lifts off as emulsion droplets.

nodes.label: Hair Conditioning
nodes.summary: Positively charged cationic surfactants/polymers attach to net-negatively charged hair, easing brushing and improving appearance.

nodes.label: Dispersant Demand Study
nodes.summary: Determines optimum dispersant level, giving lowest dispersion viscosity, for inorganic particles in foundations and sunscreens.

nodes.label: Zwitterionic Point
nodes.summary: Narrow pH range where amphoteric surfactants show nonionic character; formulating there should be avoided.

nodes.label: Krafft Temperature
nodes.summary: Temperature above which certain lipophilic surfactant emulsifiers form lamellar liquid crystals in water.

nodes.label: Shampoo
nodes.summary: Typically anionic sulfate (6-12%) plus amphoteric/betaine (~5%) plus nonionic amide (~2%) plus salt for viscosity; sulfate-free poses challenges.

nodes.label: Hair Conditioner
nodes.summary: Built with long-alkyl-chain cationic surfactant, fatty alcohol for viscosity, and ethoxylated fatty alcohol; usually <10% solids.

nodes.label: Skin Cleanser
nodes.summary: Formulated like shampoos; facial cleansers use milder anionics; body washes add emollients for moisturization.

nodes.label: Creams and Lotions
nodes.summary: Emulsions using 1-5% emulsifiers, generally anionic or nonionic.

nodes.label: Antiperspirant
nodes.summary: Roll-ons are difficult emulsions (low viscosity, low pH, high electrolyte); use blends of low/high HLB ethoxylated fatty alcohols.

nodes.label: Liquid Foundation
nodes.summary: Often water-in-silicone emulsions using silicone nonionic emulsifiers and dispersants for pigments.

nodes.label: Sulfates
nodes.summary: Anionics made by sulfating alcohols or alcohol ethoxylates; outstanding foam; ethoxylation decreases irritation and foam.

nodes.label: Sodium Lauryl Sulfate
nodes.summary: Typical sulfate anionic surfactant used in shampoos and body washes.

nodes.label: Sodium Laureth Sulfate
nodes.summary: Typical ethoxylated sulfate anionic surfactant.

nodes.label: Sulfonates
nodes.summary: Anionics from sulfonation of alpha olefins, used in hand wash; stable over wide pH.

nodes.label: Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate
nodes.summary: Typical sulfonate surfactant.

nodes.label: Phosphate Esters
nodes.summary: Anionics made by phosphation of alcohols; emulsifiers in sunscreens, stable over wider pH than soap; rich lubricious foams.

nodes.label: Potassium Cetyl Phosphate
nodes.summary: Phosphate ester emulsifier.

nodes.label: Sarcosinates
nodes.summary: Mild foaming anionic surfactants from acyl chloride and N-methyl glycine; compatible with cationics.

nodes.label: Glutamates
nodes.summary: Very mild anionic surfactants (e.g. sodium cocoyl glutamate) acceptable for natural formulations.

nodes.label: Sodium Cocoyl Glutamate
nodes.summary: Typical glutamate surfactant.

nodes.label: Lactylates
nodes.summary: Reaction products of fatty acid and lactic acid; emulsifiers and foam boosters; seen as naturally derived.

nodes.label: Sodium Stearoyl Lactylate
nodes.summary: Lactylate emulsifier.

nodes.label: Isethionates
nodes.summary: Mild esters of isethionic acid and fatty acids used in syndet bars.

nodes.label: Sodium Cocoyl Isethionate
nodes.summary: Typical isethionate surfactant.

nodes.label: Taurates
nodes.summary: Mild anionics for opaque shampoos (e.g. sodium methyl cocoyl taurate).

nodes.label: Carboxylates
nodes.summary: Mild anionics used to reduce eye irritation of other anionics.

nodes.label: Sulfosuccinates
nodes.summary: Anionic class, e.g. disodium laureth sulfosuccinate.

nodes.label: Alkanolamides
nodes.summary: Nonionic amides from triglycerides and MEA/DEA; manage salt thickening, solubilize fragrance, stabilize foam; DEA disfavored for toxicology.

nodes.label: Cocamide MEA
nodes.summary: Typical alkanolamide.

nodes.label: Cocamide DEA
nodes.summary: Alkanolamide; DEA-based materials have fallen into disfavor over toxicological concerns.

nodes.label: Ethoxylated Fatty Alcohols
nodes.summary: Nonionic emulsifiers in creams, roll-ons and conditioners; low and high HLB variants (Steareth-2, Steareth-21, Laureth-23).

nodes.label: Steareth-20
nodes.summary: Nonionic with hydrophilic head 75% of weight, HLB 15.

nodes.label: Glyceryl and Polyglyceryl Esters
nodes.summary: Nonionic emulsifiers; glyceryl esters low HLB; polyglyceryl esters effective W/O emulsifiers.

nodes.label: Glyceryl Stearate
nodes.summary: Typical glyceryl ester emulsifier.

nodes.label: PEG-Esters
nodes.summary: Normally high HLB nonionic emulsifiers (PEG-100 stearate).

nodes.label: Silicone Copolyols
nodes.summary: Dimethicone with EO/PO added; powerful W/Si and W/O emulsifiers for foundations and sunscreens.

nodes.label: Alkyl Polyglucosides
nodes.summary: Fatty alcohol + glucose; mild foamers, natural alternatives to ethoxylates; decyl, lauryl, cetearyl glucoside.

nodes.label: Decyl Glucoside
nodes.summary: Typical alkyl polyglucoside.

nodes.label: Polysorbates
nodes.summary: Sorbitan esters reacted with ethylene oxide; high HLB emulsifiers and solubilizers; reduce eye sting in baby shampoos.

nodes.label: Polysorbate 80
nodes.summary: High HLB (14.9) nonionic used in required-HLB test blends.

nodes.label: Sorbitan Esters
nodes.summary: Sorbitol + fatty acids; low HLB emulsifiers; can form liquid crystals; first nonionics (1930s).

nodes.label: Sorbitan Oleate
nodes.summary: Low HLB (4.3) nonionic used in required-HLB test blends.

nodes.label: Poloxamers
nodes.summary: ABA EO-PO-EO block copolymers; solubilizers and gelling agents in oral care (Poloxamer 407, 188).

nodes.label: Betaines
nodes.summary: Mild, good-foaming surfactants classed as amphoteric though technically cationic; from alkylation of tertiary amine with chloroacetic acid.

nodes.label: Cocamidopropyl Betaine
nodes.summary: Typical betaine surfactant.

nodes.label: Amphoacetates
nodes.summary: Amphoterics from carboxymethylation of fatty imidazoline; irritation reduction, light conditioning.

nodes.label: Quaternary Ammonium Compounds
nodes.summary: Primary conditioning agents in rinse-off conditioners; made by reacting tertiary amine with alkylating agent.

nodes.label: Cetrimonium Chloride
nodes.summary: Typical quaternary ammonium conditioning agent.

nodes.label: Behentrimonium Methosulfate
nodes.summary: Typical quaternary ammonium conditioning agent.

nodes.label: Alkyl Amines
nodes.summary: Amidopropyl amines protonated below pH 7 to give cationic character; used in conditioners.

nodes.label: Stearamidopropyl Dimethylamine
nodes.summary: Typical amidopropyl amine conditioner.

nodes.label: Amine Oxides
nodes.summary: Foam stabilizers, viscosity boosters, solubilizers made by oxidation of tertiary amines.

nodes.label: Skin Irritation
nodes.summary: Cationic and anionic surfactants have the highest irritation potential.

nodes.label: Eye Irritation
nodes.summary: Anionics can cause eye irritation; reduced by carboxylates and polysorbates.

nodes.label: William C. Griffin
nodes.summary: Designed the HLB system to guide use of nonionic surfactants.

nodes.label: Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Silicone backbone to which EO/PO are added to make silicone copolyol emulsifiers.

nodes.label: Lactic Acid
nodes.summary: Reacted with fatty acids to form lactylate surfactants.

nodes.label: Sunscreen
nodes.summary: Uses phosphate ester and silicone copolyol emulsifiers and dispersants for inorganic particles.

nodes.label: Oral Care Products
nodes.summary: Poloxamers used as solubilizers and gelling agents in oral care.

nodes.label: Skin Lipid Barrier
nodes.summary: Lipid bilayers in upper skin layers; hydrophilic surfactants can disrupt them.

nodes.label: Ingredients for Creating the Next Greatest Lipstick
nodes.summary: Explains lipstick as a crystalline wax-oil stick and the conflicting attributes of comfort, shine and long wear. Reviews traditional waxes, esters and castor oil, then new technologies: sugar esters, novel plant and silicone waxes, alkyl and phenyl silicones, elastomers, film formers, rainforest ingredients, powder fillers, effect pigments and colorants.

nodes.label: Lipstick
nodes.summary: Crystalline solid of waxes, oils and colorants molded into a swivel cartridge; ~2000 shade names across 50+ US brands; sales up ~15% in 2011; melt point should be 65-75°C.

nodes.label: Lipstick Molding
nodes.summary: Metal book molds (requiring flaming to remove seams) or silicone molds allowing unusual shapes without flaming; silicone ingredients can cause problems in silicone molds.

nodes.label: Holy Grail of Lipsticks
nodes.summary: Combining comfort, high shine and long wear (at least 4-6 h) in one product; attributes are contradictory since shine is a function of melt.

nodes.label: Candelilla Wax
nodes.summary: Euphorbia cerifera wax; typical lipstick hard wax needed for strength and shine.

nodes.label: Carnauba Wax
nodes.summary: Copernicia cerifera wax; typical lipstick hard wax for strength and shine.

nodes.label: Beeswax
nodes.summary: White beeswax (Cera Alba) used in lipstick for stick shrinkage and mold release; synthetic grades available.

nodes.label: Waxes
nodes.summary: Key lipstick component providing crystalline structure; hard waxes melt over ~3-5°C range, soft waxes over ~10-12°C.

nodes.label: Microcrystalline Wax
nodes.summary: Amorphous mineral-based hard wax used in lipsticks.

nodes.label: Ozokerite
nodes.summary: Hydrocarbon wax whose phase transition behavior silicone waxes resemble.

nodes.label: Castor Oil
nodes.summary: Ricinus communis seed oil; inexpensive polar solvent and good pigment-wetting agent; main solvent to grind pigments but not obligatory.

nodes.label: Esters
nodes.summary: Most common lipstick ingredients; thousands possible from different acids and alcohols, from light penetrating to heavy pastes.

nodes.label: Sugar Esters of Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Sucrose reacted with fatty acids (sucrose distearate, palmitate, cocoate); natural, approved food additives; reduce water loss and aid lip adhesion.

nodes.label: Sucrose Distearate
nodes.summary: Common sucrose fatty acid ester in cosmetics.

nodes.label: Essential Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Omega-3, -6 and -9 unsaturated fatty acids from seed/nut oils; aesthetic and restorative claims.

nodes.label: Linoleic Acid
nodes.summary: Omega-6 unsaturated fatty acid found in seed and nut oils.

nodes.label: Linolenic Acid
nodes.summary: Omega-3 unsaturated fatty acid found in plant seed oils.

nodes.label: Oleic Acid
nodes.summary: Omega-9 fatty acid, major component of olive oil.

nodes.label: Omega-7 Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: Unsaturated at seven carbons from chain end; rich in macadamia nut and sea buckthorn oils.

nodes.label: Kukui Nut Oil
nodes.summary: High in omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids.

nodes.label: Macadamia Nut Oil
nodes.summary: Rich source of omega-7 fatty acids.

nodes.label: Sea Buckthorn Oil
nodes.summary: Rich source of omega-7 fatty acids.

nodes.label: Olive Oil
nodes.summary: Major source of oleic acid (omega-9).

nodes.label: Bis-Diglyceryl Polyacyladipate-2
nodes.summary: High-viscosity alkyl ester offering creaminess and skin protection via film forming.

nodes.label: New Plant Waxes
nodes.summary: Neem, esparto, bayberry, sunflower, jojoba, rice bran waxes and castor-based polyester waxes offered as lipstick points of difference.

nodes.label: Silicone Waxes
nodes.summary: Phase transition at or slightly above room temperature giving creamy laydown; higher MW than paraffin, compatible with paraffin waxes.

nodes.label: Silicones
nodes.summary: Growing integral class of cosmetic ingredients offering characteristics unavailable from conventional ingredients.

nodes.label: Alkyl Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Alkyl-modified silicones soluble in oils and petrolatum, insoluble in dimethicone; hardness/melt point rise with alkyl length (C32+ melt ≥60°C).

nodes.label: Silicone Elastomers
nodes.summary: Elastomer particles in silicone carrier gels or powders; excellent film formers, first used medically; range of viscosities and tack.

nodes.label: Polysilicone-11
nodes.summary: Silicone compound listed as adding positive feel and performance to lipsticks.

nodes.label: Trimethylsiloxyphenyl Dimethicone
nodes.summary: Phenyl-modified silicone with higher refractive index for more shine; reduces tack of acrylic polymers.

nodes.label: Siliconyl Waxes
nodes.summary: Silicone-modified beeswax, carnauba, candelilla and polyethylene that improve compatibility of silicones in formulas.

nodes.label: Bentonite
nodes.summary: Clay pre-dispersed in solvent as master gel; reduces molecular movement and sweating in lipsticks; rheology control.

nodes.label: Hectorite
nodes.summary: Clay used as master gel in lipsticks to reduce sweating and control rheology.

nodes.label: Lipstick Sweating
nodes.summary: Liquid droplets appear on stick from molecular movement at elevated temperature or ingredient incompatibility; reduced by clay gels.

nodes.label: Drop Point
nodes.summary: Relative measure of a product's melt viscosity, differing from melt point.

nodes.label: Rheology
nodes.summary: Important lipstick parameter to inhibit flow at elevated temperatures; altered by clays.

nodes.label: Polybutene
nodes.summary: Synthetic giving extremely high shine but very tacky on lips.

nodes.label: Hydrogenated Polyisobutene
nodes.summary: Maintains high shine of polybutenes but much less tacky.

nodes.label: Rainforest Ingredients
nodes.summary: Exotic ingredients from Amazon, Africa and Asia (copaiba balsam, andiroba oil, dragon's blood, açai butter, buriti oil, maracuja oil) adding moisturization, emolliency and shine.

nodes.label: Copaiba Balsam
nodes.summary: Rainforest ingredient trending in lipsticks.

nodes.label: Andiroba Oil
nodes.summary: Rainforest oil trending in color cosmetics.

nodes.label: Açai Butter
nodes.summary: Rainforest butter used in lipsticks.

nodes.label: Rainforest Loss
nodes.summary: Disappearance of rainforests removes sources of ingredients that may grow only there.

nodes.label: Spreading Coefficient
nodes.summary: Measure of ingredient spreadability; increases with polarity, MW and branching; silicone oils ≥35.

nodes.label: Mineral Oil
nodes.summary: Hydrocarbon that feels dry with little slip; occlusive and moisturizing but adds little aesthetics; many formulators avoid it.

nodes.label: Triisostearyl Citrate
nodes.summary: Moderate MW ester offering more creaminess and shine than hydrocarbons.

nodes.label: PVP/Eicosene Copolymer
nodes.summary: Ganex V220 oil-soluble film former, originally for hair shine, increasing lipstick wear.

nodes.label: Film Formers
nodes.summary: Polymers that extend wear but are often stiff and uncomfortable on lips.

nodes.label: Boron Nitride
nodes.summary: Synthetic ceramic powder with lamellar structure that glides; made from borax and nitrogen source; not natural despite name.

nodes.label: Polymethyl Methacrylate
nodes.summary: Spherical powder filler providing ball-bearing slip.

nodes.label: Polytetrafluoroethylene
nodes.summary: Specialty powder filler giving smooth slippery feel.

nodes.label: Spherical Silica
nodes.summary: Nonabsorbent spherical powder providing ball-bearing effect.

nodes.label: Nylon-12
nodes.summary: Synthetic nylon powder enhancing feel and application.

nodes.label: Silk Powder
nodes.summary: Natural powder derived from silk protein to enhance feel.

nodes.label: Calcium Aluminum Borosilicate
nodes.summary: Smooth flat glass-like effect pigment enhancing lipstick feel.

nodes.label: Lauroyl Lysine
nodes.summary: Amino acid powder texture modifier with slippery feel.

nodes.label: Mica
nodes.summary: Effect pigment with irregular jagged platelets; size restricted ≤150 microns in some eye products.

nodes.label: PET Glitter
nodes.summary: Polyethylene terephthalate glitter pearls; large, hygroscopic, felt on lips.

nodes.label: Color Additives
nodes.summary: Colorants depositing color; some (D&C Red 6/7 lakes, yellow iron oxide) have high oil absorbance; ground in castor oil via ball or three-roll mill.

nodes.label: Bromofluorescein Staining Dyes
nodes.summary: Lakes of D&C Red 22, 28 and Orange 5; pH-sensitive dyes staining lips pink to extend wear; hygroscopic and may dry lips.

nodes.label: Titanium Dioxide
nodes.summary: Colorant with relatively low oil absorbance.

nodes.label: Iron Oxides
nodes.summary: Yellow iron oxide has fairly high oil absorbance.

nodes.label: Oil Absorbance
nodes.summary: Calculated per standard ASTM method; balanced with alumina hydrate or barium sulfate.

nodes.label: Lipstick Crush (Snap) Test
nodes.summary: Crushing stick between fingers should give resistance and a snap, indicating sufficient crystallinity; alternative to Chatillon.

nodes.label: Lipstick Crystalline Structure
nodes.summary: Strong wax crystalline matrix needed for stick strength; excessive pigment loading turns it amorphous and breaks at cup line.

nodes.label: Me-Too Products
nodes.summary: Products differing only in ingredient combinations rather than new technology; new technology is the point of difference.

nodes.label: GRAS
nodes.summary: Generally Recognized as Safe; most sweeteners, flavorings and maskants in lip products are GRAS.

nodes.label: Lips
nodes.summary: Substrate for lipstick; thin layer of moisture present; hygroscopic ingredients can dry them.

nodes.label: Hyaluronan: A Natural Moisturizer
nodes.summary: Describes the structure and physicochemical properties of hyaluronan, preparation and characterization of HA fragments and chemical derivatives, skin penetration as a function of molecular weight, and molecular-weight-dependent moisturizing and anti-aging effects in cosmetics.

nodes.label: Glucuronic Acid
nodes.summary: Monosaccharide unit of hyaluronan, β-1,3-linked.

nodes.label: N-Acetyl-D-Glucosamine
nodes.summary: Monosaccharide unit of hyaluronan; found at reducing end of enzymatically produced fragments.

nodes.label: Extracellular Matrix
nodes.summary: HA is a main ECM component in connective, epithelial and neural tissues; high-MW HA contributes to its structure.

nodes.label: Hyaluronan Fragments
nodes.summary: Low-MW HA oligosaccharides; 6-20 units are pro-angiogenic; <5 kDa suppress wrinkles; ≤50 kDa act as signals for new HA synthesis.

nodes.label: Hyaluronidase
nodes.summary: Enzyme degrading HA (bovine testicular hyaluronidase gives saturated even-numbered oligomers); recognizes the carboxyl group.

nodes.label: Hyaluronate Lyase
nodes.summary: Enzyme producing unsaturated even-numbered HA oligosaccharides.

nodes.label: Hyaluronan Degradation
nodes.summary: Cleavage by enzymatic, free radical, thermal, ultrasonic, acid and alkaline methods; native HA has low enzymatic resistance and short half-life.

nodes.label: Angiogenesis
nodes.summary: Development of new blood vessels; stimulated by HA oligosaccharides of 6-20 units.

nodes.label: Fibroblast
nodes.summary: HA fragments support fibroblast proliferation.

nodes.label: Endothelial Cell
nodes.summary: Cells lining blood vessels; HA oligosaccharides are mitogenic for them.

nodes.label: Hair Loss
nodes.summary: HA oligosaccharides are components of compositions combating hair loss and stimulating hair growth.

nodes.label: Wrinkles
nodes.summary: HA fragments treat and prevent wrinkles; decline of HA with age leads to wrinkles.

nodes.label: Interleukins
nodes.summary: Pro-inflammatory polypeptides generating free radicals; decreased by HA fragments in dermis.

nodes.label: Free Radicals
nodes.summary: Damage ECM and skin cells; generated via pro-inflammatory interleukins; also degrade HA.

nodes.label: Electrospray Ionization Mass Spectrometry
nodes.summary: Characterizes MW of short HA oligomers up to 40-mer; cone voltage must be set carefully to avoid artifacts.

nodes.label: MALDI-TOF
nodes.summary: Mass spectrometry suitable for polydisperse HA mixtures, salt tolerant and sensitive but not quantitative.

nodes.label: Size-Exclusion Chromatography with Multi-Angle Light Scattering
nodes.summary: SEC-MALS-RI gives MW, distribution and size of HA fragments; two columns in series improve separation.

nodes.label: Hyaluronan Chemical Modification
nodes.summary: Attaching pendant groups (via carboxyl, hydroxyl or amino) or cross-linking to improve enzymatic resistance, robustness and skin binding; degradation inevitable.

nodes.label: Hyaluronan Cross-Linking
nodes.summary: Forms insoluble HA hydrogels with longer residence and robustness; most commercial HA products are cross-linked (e.g. divinyl sulfone in Juvederm).

nodes.label: Carbodiimide Coupling
nodes.summary: EDC, CDI, NHS and similar peptide-synthesis reagents activate HA carboxyls to form amide or ester bonds; preferably in water.

nodes.label: Divinyl Sulfone
nodes.summary: Cross-linker used in commercial Juvederm HA filler.

nodes.label: Dermal Filler
nodes.summary: Cross-linked HA such as Juvederm used in cosmetic surgery; allergic reactions have been reported.

nodes.label: Hydrogel Swelling Ratio
nodes.summary: Measures water retention of HA hydrogels; low degree of substitution gives high swelling.

nodes.label: Shear Modulus
nodes.summary: G measures mechanical integrity of HA hydrogels; increases with HA modification.

nodes.label: Hydrophobized Hyaluronan
nodes.summary: HA modified with hydrophobic groups (e.g. 50 kDa HA with 50% hexyl groups) to enhance SC penetration; enhanced hydration comparably to 17 kDa HA; can form micro/nano vehicles.

nodes.label: Stratum Corneum
nodes.summary: Hydrophobic outer skin layer; hydrophobic small HA fragments theoretically penetrate it better.

nodes.label: Epidermis
nodes.summary: HA most prominent in upper spinous and granular layers (extracellular); epidermal HA disappears in senile skin.

nodes.label: Dermis
nodes.summary: Contains most skin HA, in equilibrium with lymphatic and vascular systems; level remains constant with aging.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte
nodes.summary: Basal keratinocyte HA is intracellular and involved in cell cycling.

nodes.label: Skin
nodes.summary: Largest reservoir of HA, holding 50% of total body HA.

nodes.label: Franz Diffusion Cell
nodes.summary: Used with 14C-HA on porcine ear skin at 37°C for 48 h; 357 kDa HA taken up by epidermis but hardly into dermis.

nodes.label: Skin Penetration
nodes.summary: HA >500 kDa does not penetrate and forms barrier films; smaller fragments permeate; permeability inversely related to size.

nodes.label: Transepidermal Water Loss
nodes.summary: Lowered by high-MW HA films on upper epidermis.

nodes.label: Skin Hydration
nodes.summary: In a 60-day study with 0.005% HA, 4.6 and 17 kDa fragments raised hydration first month; 1.66 MDa HA best after three months.

nodes.label: Natural Moisturizing Factor
nodes.summary: Hygroscopic substances, including HA, that buffer skin and preserve appearance.

nodes.label: Glycerin
nodes.summary: Common humectant whose moisturizing depends on humidity; at low humidity draws water from inner skin.

nodes.label: Propylene Glycol
nodes.summary: Common moisturizer influenced by relative humidity.

nodes.label: Humectants
nodes.summary: Moisturizers such as glycerin, propylene glycol, sorbitol, PEG; HA retains water at low and high humidity unlike others.

nodes.label: Differential Scanning Calorimetry
nodes.summary: DSC estimates non-freezable bound, freezable bound and free water around HA; 650 kDa HA binds 7.6 non-freezable and up to 43 freezable water per disaccharide.

nodes.label: Bound Water
nodes.summary: Non-freezable and freezable bound water hydrating HA; 1 g of 650 kDa HA holds 0.8-2 g water; independent of MW from 30-750 kDa.

nodes.label: Hair Keratin
nodes.summary: HA restructures keratin fibers inside hair, improving elasticity and wash resistance of colored hair.

nodes.label: Transdermal Delivery
nodes.summary: HA enhances partitioning of diclofenac and ibuprofen into skin; HA-based liposomes, microemulsions and micelles can more than double penetration.

nodes.label: Penetration Enhancers
nodes.summary: Combining with high-MW HA improves its penetration and anti-aging effect.

nodes.label: Skin Elasticity
nodes.summary: Decreases with declining HA production during aging.

nodes.label: Skin Barrier Function
nodes.summary: Improved by HA in formulations; high-MW HA forms barrier against moisture loss.

nodes.label: Cancer
nodes.summary: HA oligosaccharides sensitize cancer cells to treatment and inhibit pro-tumorigenic signaling of high-MW HA.

nodes.label: Serum
nodes.summary: Typical cosmetic product supplemented with HA.

nodes.label: Ayurveda in Personal Care
nodes.summary: Introduces Ayurveda, the ancient Indian holistic medicine system based on doshas and plant ingredients, and its relevance to green personal care. Reviews Ayurvedic botanicals with antioxidant (amla), anti-inflammatory (turmeric/curcumin) and antimicrobial (neem, triphala) benefits.

nodes.label: Ayurveda
nodes.summary: Ancient Indian holistic medicine ('knowledge for long life') using plant-derived ingredients, treating cause not symptom with individualized therapy; ~1200 plants described.

nodes.label: Doshas
nodes.summary: Basic energy types: Vata (air, motion), Pitta (bile, metabolism), Kapha (phlegm, growth); imbalance from genetics, stress, diet.

nodes.label: Panchakarma
nodes.summary: Ayurvedic bio-purification using oil or water based extract blends for dermatological concerns, with oral supplements and poultices.

nodes.label: Beauty from Within
nodes.summary: Ayurveda is argued to pioneer the concept, combining topical treatment with oral supplements.

nodes.label: Reactive Oxygen Species
nodes.summary: Damage DNA, proteins, lipids, saccharides; increased by pollution, UV, stress, smoking; drive inflammation and premature aging.

nodes.label: Superoxide Dismutase
nodes.summary: Most important endogenous enzyme for mitigating reactive oxygen.

nodes.label: Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Herbal antioxidants protect skin from ROS; Ayurvedic sources rich in vitamin C, phenolic acids and bioflavonoids.

nodes.label: Amla
nodes.summary: Phyllanthus emblica; among richest vitamin C sources, high tannins; actives gallic and ellagic acid; mitigates UVA/UVB photodamage.

nodes.label: Ashwagandha
nodes.summary: Withania somnifera; successfully used Ayurvedic antioxidant.

nodes.label: Guduchi
nodes.summary: Tinospora cordifolia; Ayurvedic antioxidant.

nodes.label: Licorice
nodes.summary: Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra); Ayurvedic antioxidant.

nodes.label: Vidarikanda
nodes.summary: Pueraria tuberosa; Ayurvedic antioxidant.

nodes.label: Gallic Acid
nodes.summary: Primary active component of amla.

nodes.label: Ellagic Acid
nodes.summary: Primary active component of amla.

nodes.label: Vitamin C
nodes.summary: Antioxidant abundant in amla and other Ayurvedic botanicals.

nodes.label: Tannins
nodes.summary: Present in amla; antioxidant and anti-inflammatory.

nodes.label: Inflammation
nodes.summary: Complex cellular response, acute or chronic; triggered by UV, stress, infection, impaired stratum corneum and ROS; linked to collagen/elastin breakdown and skin aging.

nodes.label: Photodamage
nodes.summary: Skin damage from UVA and UVB exposure, mitigated by amla.

nodes.label: UV Radiation
nodes.summary: UVA/UVB environmental stressor triggering ROS and inflammatory cascade.

nodes.label: Collagen
nodes.summary: Critical ECM protein broken down in inflammation-driven aging; protected by curcuminoids.

nodes.label: Elastin
nodes.summary: ECM protein broken down by inflammation; protected by curcuminoids.

nodes.label: Matrix Metalloproteinases
nodes.summary: Increased by inflammatory cascade, contributing to ECM breakdown.

nodes.label: Turmeric
nodes.summary: Ayurvedic herb with anti-inflammatory and antiseptic benefits; source of curcumin.

nodes.label: Curcumin
nodes.summary: Curcuminoid secondary metabolite of turmeric; modulates TNFα, NFκB, COX2, IL1; protects collagen and elastin; antioxidant and may suppress cancers.

nodes.label: NF-κB
nodes.summary: Key inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.

nodes.label: TNF-α
nodes.summary: Inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.

nodes.label: COX-2
nodes.summary: Inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.

nodes.label: Bacopa Monnieri
nodes.summary: Bhrami; Ayurvedic anti-inflammatory ingredient.

nodes.label: Eclipta Alba
nodes.summary: Bhringraj; Ayurvedic anti-inflammatory ingredient.

nodes.label: Swertia Chirata
nodes.summary: Chirata; Ayurvedic anti-inflammatory.

nodes.label: Acne
nodes.summary: Result of microbial infection by Propionibacterium acnes; Ayurvedic products tested clinically.

nodes.label: Dandruff
nodes.summary: Scalp condition caused primarily by Malassezia furfur.

nodes.label: Propionibacterium acnes
nodes.summary: Pathogenic microorganism causing acne.

nodes.label: Malassezia furfur
nodes.summary: Yeast primarily responsible for scalp infection causing dandruff.

nodes.label: Neem
nodes.summary: Azadirachta indica; over 100 actives purified; antimicrobial against S. aureus, E. coli, P. aeruginosa, C. albicans, A. niger; used in oral care.

nodes.label: Triphala
nodes.summary: Ayurvedic blend of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaka (Terminalia belerica) and Amalaki; tonic to control microbial infection.

nodes.label: Terminalia Chebula
nodes.summary: Haritaki, component of Triphala.

nodes.label: Terminalia Bellirica
nodes.summary: Bibhitaka, component of Triphala.

nodes.label: Antimicrobials
nodes.summary: Compounds controlling microbes; Ayurvedic botanicals can serve as natural preservatives.

nodes.label: Natural Preservatives
nodes.summary: Industry moving towards sustainable natural preservatives; Ayurvedic ingredients could be high-value.

nodes.label: Staphylococcus aureus
nodes.summary: Pathogen controlled by neem extracts.

nodes.label: Candida albicans
nodes.summary: Pathogenic yeast controlled by neem extracts.

nodes.label: Oral Care Products
nodes.summary: Neem bark used for antimicrobial oral and dental care.

nodes.label: Green and Sustainable Personal Care
nodes.summary: European and North American consumers trend towards sustainable green care; Ayurveda offers holistic botanical approach.

nodes.label: Randomized Controlled Trials
nodes.summary: Large-population controlled efficacy evaluation needed to validate Ayurvedic medicine.

nodes.label: Probiotics in Topical Personal Healthcare
nodes.summary: Argues live organisms are not required for probiotic bioactivity and proposes the term Probiotic Derived Bioactive. Explains how microbial molecules such as beta-1,3-D-glucans, lipoteichoic acid and peptidoglycans activate toll-like receptors on keratinocytes to produce antimicrobial defensins, and how in vitro epithelial models with ELISA test efficacy.

nodes.label: Probiotics
nodes.summary: WHO: live microorganisms conferring health benefit in adequate amounts; author proposes 'live or dead'; includes Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Saccharomyces boulardii, Streptococcus thermophilus strains.

nodes.label: Probiotic Derived Bioactive
nodes.summary: Isolated ingredient from a probiotic organism shown to be bioactive (immune-stimulating, anti-inflammatory); INCI names end in ferment, extract or lysate.

nodes.label: Lactobacillus
nodes.summary: Probiotic genus (acidophilus, casei, lactis, plantarum, reuteri, rhamnosus, helveticus); L. acidophilus cell wall has lipoteichoic acid and peptidoglycans.

nodes.label: Bifidobacterium
nodes.summary: Probiotic genus (formerly Lactobacillus bifidus).

nodes.label: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
nodes.summary: Brewers' yeast, arguably probiotic; yeast cell walls source of beta-glucans.

nodes.label: Beta-1,3-D-Glucan
nodes.summary: Yeast cell-wall polysaccharide used ~70 years as nutraceutical and skincare additive; identified by DiLuzio as active of zymosan; stimulates immunity via Dectin-1; primary PDB.

nodes.label: Zymosan
nodes.summary: Isolated from yeast cell walls by Louis Pillemer in the 1940s; immune-stimulating.

nodes.label: Lipoteichoic Acid
nodes.summary: Lactobacillus cell-wall molecule associated with immune stimulation via TLR2.

nodes.label: Peptidoglycan
nodes.summary: Bacterial cell-wall molecule eliciting immune-cell stimulation.

nodes.label: Defensins
nodes.summary: Antimicrobial host defense peptides discovered mid-1980s, produced by epithelial cells (trachea, bowel, epidermis); also proliferative and anti-inflammatory; overproduced in psoriasis.

nodes.label: Toll-Like Receptors
nodes.summary: Pattern recognition receptors (~11 characterized) on epithelia, keratinocytes and Langerhans cells; activation causes defensin production.

nodes.label: Pattern Recognition Receptors
nodes.summary: Receptors on epithelial cells recognizing microbial components; discovered mid-1990s.

nodes.label: Dectin-1
nodes.summary: Surface receptor needed for full response to fungal beta-glucans (Brown et al. 2003).

nodes.label: Innate Immunity
nodes.summary: First-line defense requiring no prior exposure; epithelial surfaces form 'one big immune system'.

nodes.label: Langerhans Cell
nodes.summary: Skin immune cells bearing toll-like receptors.

nodes.label: Macrophage
nodes.summary: Second-line cellular immune defense stimulated by defensins.

nodes.label: Quantitative PCR
nodes.summary: Enabled in vivo testing of host peptide up-regulation by PDBs.

nodes.label: ELISA
nodes.summary: Monitors defensin levels in epithelial cultures before/after test candidates; semi-quantitative.

nodes.label: In Vitro Epithelial Cell Models
nodes.summary: Models (Mattek, Skin Sensitive) mimicking oral and nasal linings that produce defensins; alternative to animal testing.

nodes.label: Rosette Test
nodes.summary: Former small-animal test of immune activation not directly measuring defensins.

nodes.label: Alternatives to Animal Testing
nodes.summary: In vitro epithelial models with ELISA give rapid alternative to animal testing for probiotic efficacy.

nodes.label: Psoriasis
nodes.summary: Condition in which defensins are overproduced, so topical probiotics may be unsuitable.

nodes.label: World Health Organization
nodes.summary: Provides the standard probiotic definition.

nodes.label: Fermented Foods
nodes.summary: Yogurt, buttermilk, miso, sauerkraut, kefir; probiotic foods used for millennia.

nodes.label: Green and Sustainable Bioactives from Biofermentation
nodes.summary: Describes fermentation and cell culture (submerged and solid-state) as sustainable means of producing cosmetic bioactives from yeast, Lactobacillus, fungi, algae and plant meristem cultures. Covers environmental advantages over chemical synthesis and activities such as live yeast cell derivatives, algal MMP and tyrosinase inhibitors, plant stem cell extracts, flavonoids and recombinant peptides and hyaluronic acid.

nodes.label: Fermentation
nodes.summary: Biotransformation of simple nutrients (sugars) by organisms into secondary metabolites, vitamins, enzymes, peptides; used since 3000 BCE; sustainable route to cosmetic bioactives.

nodes.label: Submerged Fermentation
nodes.summary: Liquid media in enclosed stainless tanks; nutrients used quickly, robust growth and easy purification.

nodes.label: Solid-State Fermentation
nodes.summary: Carbon-rich solids (bran, paper pulp) used slowly; recyclable nutrient source; common for fungi and food-waste biomass.

nodes.label: Plant Cell Culture
nodes.summary: Meristem/callus cultures producing high-value compounds sustainably (carotenoids, flavonoids) without field-grown biomass, pesticides or herbicides.

nodes.label: Aspergillus oryzae
nodes.summary: Koji mold; well-developed fungal fermentation vehicle, along with Aspergillus niger.

nodes.label: Microalgae
nodes.summary: Spirulina, Ulkenia, Chlorella fermented in bioreactors for secondary metabolites.

nodes.label: Stressed Lysates
nodes.summary: Organisms grown under heat shock, peroxide or UV stress produce enhanced novel actives.

nodes.label: Dual Fermentation
nodes.summary: Growing multiple organisms simultaneously for bioactive expression with potential anti-aging benefits.

nodes.label: Live Yeast Cell Derivative
nodes.summary: LYCD from S. cerevisiae; increases tissue respiration and accelerates wound healing; peptide fractions stimulate cell renewal.

nodes.label: Wound Healing
nodes.summary: Accelerated by S. cerevisiae lysates.

nodes.label: Skin Cell Renewal
nodes.summary: Yeast peptide fractions stimulate skin-cell renewal via increased metabolic activity.

nodes.label: Bacteriocins
nodes.summary: Short-chain antimicrobial peptides from bacteria used to manage acne.

nodes.label: Phlorotannins
nodes.summary: Marine algal compounds with topical skin applications.

nodes.label: Sulfated Polysaccharides
nodes.summary: Marine algal compounds used in skin formulations.

nodes.label: Corallina pilulifera Extract
nodes.summary: Marine alga extract preventing UV-induced oxidative stress and MMP-2/MMP-9 expression in dermal fibroblasts.

nodes.label: Fucoxanthin
nodes.summary: Carotenoid from Laminaria japonica that suppresses tyrosinase activity, suggesting skin lightening.

nodes.label: Chlorella Extract
nodes.summary: Green microalga extract inhibiting MMP1 activity in vitro.

nodes.label: Ulkenia Extract
nodes.summary: Microalga producing lipids; extract influences skin lipid synthesis, especially cholesterol.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase
nodes.summary: Enzyme inhibited by algal compounds, fucoxanthin and peptides for skin lightening.

nodes.label: Skin Lightening
nodes.summary: Achieved via tyrosinase inhibition by algal compounds, peptides and lactic acid.

nodes.label: Oxidative Stress
nodes.summary: UV-induced oxidative stress increases MMP expression and collagen degradation.

nodes.label: Cholesterol
nodes.summary: Skin lipid whose synthesis is influenced by Ulkenia extracts.

nodes.label: Red Rice Meristem Extract
nodes.summary: Red rice callus culture extract influencing epigenetic aging factors, improving procollagen-1 and dermatopontin expression in vitro.

nodes.label: Procollagen-1
nodes.summary: Extracellular skin protein that deteriorates with age; improved by red rice callus extract.

nodes.label: Dermatopontin
nodes.summary: Extracellular skin protein declining with age; improved by red rice extract.

nodes.label: Apple Stem Cell Extract
nodes.summary: Malus domestica meristem cultures improve longevity of skin stem cells by delaying senescence.

nodes.label: Skin Stem Cells
nodes.summary: Their longevity improved by apple meristem cultures.

nodes.label: Cellular Senescence
nodes.summary: Delayed in skin stem cells by apple meristem extracts.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Regulation
nodes.summary: Red rice extracts suggest influence on epigenetic factors of aging via CpG promoter sequences.

nodes.label: Flavonoids
nodes.summary: Over 5000 plant compounds with flavane nucleus; free radical scavengers, UVA absorbing, cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory, inhibit DNA damage; e.g. quercetin, catechin, kaempferol, EGCG.

nodes.label: Quercetin
nodes.summary: Predominant dietary flavonoid.

nodes.label: Epigallocatechin Gallate
nodes.summary: Predominant dietary flavonoid (EGCG).

nodes.label: Carotenoids
nodes.summary: High-value compounds produced sustainably via plant-cell culture.

nodes.label: Resveratrol
nodes.summary: Polyphenol produced by small-molecule fermentation, bridging nutrition and personal care.

nodes.label: Peptides
nodes.summary: Recombinant peptides: tetrapeptides repress MMP-1, others inhibit tyrosinase, tripeptides influence TGF-β.

nodes.label: TGF-β
nodes.summary: Influenced by tripeptides to improve skin structure.

nodes.label: Recombinant Technology
nodes.summary: Genetically modified organisms express specific peptides and compounds, e.g. hyaluronic acid in bacteria.

nodes.label: Succinic Acid
nodes.summary: Bio-based chemical produced by fermentation as alternative to conventional chemistry.

nodes.label: Propanediol
nodes.summary: Ingredient cited as best practice for biotechnological production.

nodes.label: Sustainable Bio-Based Manufacturing
nodes.summary: Fermentation lowers CO2 emissions, uses renewable biomass waste, limits fossil fuels and pesticides, and prevents depletion of wild biomass.

nodes.label: Extremophiles
nodes.summary: Organisms from extreme environments used in fermentation.

nodes.label: Marine Algae
nodes.summary: Source of phlorotannins, sulfated polysaccharides and tyrosinase inhibitors for skin care.

nodes.label: Multi-Functional Botanicals for Topical Applications
nodes.summary: Covers natural versus naturally derived actives, extraction techniques (solvent, freeze-drying, supercritical CO2), and standardization of botanical extracts. Profiles multifunctional botanicals (amla, ellagic acid, tetrahydrocurcuminoids, coconut water, Coleus forskohlii, tetrahydropiperine, oxyresveratrol, Eclipta alba, ursolic acid, boswellic acids) with assay and clinical data, and botanical sustainability.

nodes.label: Botanical Extracts
nodes.summary: Plant extracts evolved from crude traditional preparations into pure standardized extracts validated by cell and enzyme assays; fastest-developing natural cosmetics segment.

nodes.label: Natural vs Naturally Derived Actives
nodes.summary: Naturally occurring compounds in natural form (e.g. EGCG in extract) are natural; naturally derived actives are synthesized from natural sources and don't occur in nature.

nodes.label: Solvent Extraction
nodes.summary: Most common extraction using ethanol, methanol, IPA, ethyl acetate, acetone or hexane to enrich compounds by polarity.

nodes.label: Freeze-Drying
nodes.summary: For heat-labile compounds: freezing at -40°C, primary and secondary drying; used to make Cococin coconut water solids.

nodes.label: Supercritical CO2 Extraction
nodes.summary: CO2 above 31°C and 74 bar behaves as gas and liquid; extracts nonpolar compounds from oils/oleoresins; expensive; used for coleus oil.

nodes.label: Botanical Extract Standardization
nodes.summary: AHPA: information and controls to produce materials of reasonable consistency; identify active marker, chemical fingerprinting by chromatography, ensures efficacy and authenticity.

nodes.label: American Herbal Products Association
nodes.summary: Defines standardization of botanical materials.

nodes.label: Beta Glucogallin
nodes.summary: Biomarker compound of amla identified by HPLC, LCMS, NMR; Saberry standardized to 10%.

nodes.label: ORAC Assay
nodes.summary: Oxygen Radical Absorbance Capacity; family includes ORAC hydro/lipo, HORAC, NORAC, SORAC, SOAC measuring activity against peroxyl, hydroxyl, peroxynitrite, superoxide and singlet oxygen; AOAC first action method.

nodes.label: DPPH Assay
nodes.summary: Free radical scavenging measured by absorbance decrease of DPPH radicals at 516 nm.

nodes.label: Melanogenesis
nodes.summary: Melanin synthesis catalyzed by tyrosinase (tyrosine to DOPA to DOPA-quinone); stimulated by α-MSH via cAMP-MITF.

nodes.label: B16 Melanoma Cell Melanogenesis Assay
nodes.summary: B16 F1 mouse melanoma cells induced with α-MSH or cAMP; melanin measured at 405 nm.

nodes.label: Tyrosinase Inhibition Assay
nodes.summary: In vitro mushroom tyrosinase assay on L-tyrosine measured at 475 nm.

nodes.label: Alpha-MSH
nodes.summary: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone binding melanocyte receptor, stimulating melanogenesis via cAMP-MITF.

nodes.label: MITF
nodes.summary: Microphthalmia-associated transcription factor in the cAMP melanogenesis pathway.

nodes.label: Melanocyte
nodes.summary: Melanin-producing skin cell.

nodes.label: Melanin
nodes.summary: Skin pigment reduced by ellagic acid in basal, spinous, granular and corneum layers.

nodes.label: Kojic Acid
nodes.summary: Benchmark skin lightener; tyrosinase IC50 3.0, melanogenesis IC50 100 µg/ml in comparisons.

nodes.label: Arbutin
nodes.summary: Skin lightener; tyrosinase IC50 33; less effective than ellagic acid and tetrahydrocurcuminoids.

nodes.label: Hydroquinone
nodes.summary: Potent melanin inhibitor but toxic, use restricted; 4% caused adverse reactions in 50% of subjects.

nodes.label: Procollagen
nodes.summary: Amla extract induces procollagen production in fibroblasts dose-dependently.

nodes.label: Photoaging
nodes.summary: Dermal photoaging from UV-induced MMP-1; THC with tetrahydropiperine reversed photodamage in 3-month trial.

nodes.label: Pomegranate
nodes.summary: Source of ellagic acid with antioxidant properties.

nodes.label: Japanese Quasi-Drug
nodes.summary: Functional cosmetic category in Japan requiring MHLW premarket approval; skin-lightening quasi-drugs prevent/improve melasma and chloasma.

nodes.label: Japan Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare
nodes.summary: Grants premarket approval for quasi-drugs.

nodes.label: Hyperpigmentation
nodes.summary: Pigmentation disorders such as melasma, chloasma, age spots and freckles.

nodes.label: Tetrahydrocurcumin
nodes.summary: Colorless hydrogenated metabolite of curcuminoids (Sabiwhite, INCI tetrahydrodiferuloylmethane); tyrosinase IC50 2.0, melanogenesis IC50 3.5; DPPH SC50 1.14 vs resveratrol 3.24; 0.25% outperformed 4% hydroquinone.

nodes.label: Patch Test
nodes.summary: 48-hour closed/repeat insult patch tests on 50 subjects showed no irritation for THC and tetrahydropiperine.

nodes.label: Coconut Water
nodes.summary: Liquid endosperm of Cocos nucifera rich in proteins, amino acids, vitamins, growth hormones; Cococin freeze-dried solids support fibroblast proliferation and improved skin elasticity at 1%; use 1-5%.

nodes.label: Cytokinins
nodes.summary: Plant growth substances in coconut endosperm involved in cell growth and differentiation.

nodes.label: Hair Follicle
nodes.summary: Coconut water may support growth of hair follicles; anagen phase induced by Eclipta alba.

nodes.label: Dermal Papilla Cells
nodes.summary: Mesenchymal stem cell reservoirs inducing skin appendage formation; protected from stress by Saberry+Cococin.

nodes.label: Cutometer
nodes.summary: Measures dermal elasticity; visiometer measures roughness.

nodes.label: Coleus Forskohlii
nodes.summary: Lamiaceae plant whose roots supply forskolin and antimicrobial coleus oil.

nodes.label: Forskolin
nodes.summary: Exclusive to Coleus forskohlii; direct adenylate cyclase activator raising cAMP and lipolysis without adrenergic activation; ForsLean 95% at 2-5% reduced thigh circumference 9.37% in 54 women.

nodes.label: Coleus Oil
nodes.summary: Supercritical CO2 extract of Coleus forskohlii rhizome; at 2% as effective as tea tree oil or clindamycin against P. acnes, S. aureus, S. epidermidis.

nodes.label: Tea Tree Oil
nodes.summary: Antimicrobial comparator less effective than coleus oil.

nodes.label: Adenylate Cyclase
nodes.summary: Transmembrane enzyme generating cAMP, directly activated by forskolin.

nodes.label: Cyclic AMP
nodes.summary: Second messenger activating lipase to break down fat and part of melanogenesis signaling.

nodes.label: Lipolysis
nodes.summary: Enzymatic fat breakdown in adipocytes induced via cAMP.

nodes.label: Cellulite
nodes.summary: Gynoid lipodystrophy: fat bulging through stretched collagen fibers giving orange-peel skin on hips, thighs, buttocks.

nodes.label: Adipocyte
nodes.summary: Fat cells whose excessive volume causes cellulite.

nodes.label: Tetrahydropiperine
nodes.summary: Cosmoperine: hydrogenated black pepper piperine (95%); enhances topical bioavailability (green tea +30%, forskolin +40%, BMDP diffusion in 5 min); non-irritating at 0.01-0.1%.

nodes.label: Piperine
nodes.summary: Black pepper (Piper nigrum) compound hydrogenated to tetrahydropiperine.

nodes.label: Green Tea Polyphenols
nodes.summary: Water-soluble antioxidants whose permeation is enhanced by tetrahydropiperine.

nodes.label: Oxyresveratrol
nodes.summary: Tetra-oxygenated stilbene; Artonox from Artocarpus lakoocha heartwood at 95%; tyrosinase IC50 0.049 µg/ml (140x kojic acid), 9x resveratrol; DPPH IC50 2.7; anti-inflammatory via NF-κB/COX-2.

nodes.label: Artocarpus Lakoocha
nodes.summary: Southeast Asian tree, source of 'Puag haad'; heartwood rich in oxyresveratrol.

nodes.label: Stilbenes
nodes.summary: Stilbenoids with tyrosinase inhibition depending on oxygenation; include resveratrol, oxyresveratrol, pterostilbene.

nodes.label: Elastase
nodes.summary: Enzyme breaking down elastin; oxyresveratrol IC50 120 µg/ml; human leukocyte elastase inhibited by boswellic acids.

nodes.label: Wedelolactone
nodes.summary: Main active in Eclipta alba leaves; Sabinsa extract standardized to 50%.

nodes.label: Alopecia
nodes.summary: Hair loss from scalp or body.

nodes.label: Minoxidil
nodes.summary: 2% solution used as positive control for hair growth.

nodes.label: Anagen Phase
nodes.summary: Active growth phase of hair follicles, induced by Eclipta alba.

nodes.label: Ursolic Acid
nodes.summary: Pentacyclic triterpenoid from Salvia officinalis; anti-inflammatory; liposomal form increases ceramides and collagen; improves collagen bundles and wrinkles; use 1-5%.

nodes.label: Ceramides
nodes.summary: Skin lipids increased in keratinocytes by liposomal ursolic acid.

nodes.label: Boswellic Acids
nodes.summary: From Boswellia serrata gum resin (Boswellin CG); uniquely dual-inhibit 5-lipoxygenase and human leukocyte elastase; 1% under-eye cream reduced dark circles 86% in 4 weeks.

nodes.label: 5-Lipoxygenase
nodes.summary: Converts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes; inhibited by boswellic acids.

nodes.label: Dark Under-Eye Circles
nodes.summary: Reduced by Boswellin CG under-eye cream.

nodes.label: Sustainability of Botanicals
nodes.summary: Growing demand pressures limited natural resources; crop rotation, replantation and high-yield varieties help.

nodes.label: Sabinsa Corporation
nodes.summary: Company developing standardized botanicals (Saberry, Sabiwhite, Cococin, ForsLean, Cosmoperine, Artonox, Boswellin).

nodes.label: Ingredients to Strengthen Skin Barrier Integrity
nodes.summary: Reviews epidermal barrier organization (keratinocyte differentiation, cytokeratins, desmosomes, tight junctions, dermal-epidermal junction, filaggrin) and the role of calcium signaling, which declines with aging. Presents a hydrophilic extract of the brown alga Padina pavonica that mobilizes calcium, stimulating cytokeratin and desmosome synthesis, restoring cell communication and protecting against pollutants.

nodes.label: Epidermal Layers
nodes.summary: Basal (germinal), spinous, granular, and horny (stratum corneum) layers distinguished by differentiation proteins.

nodes.label: Keratinocyte Differentiation
nodes.summary: Progressive keratinization from basal layer to surface ending in enucleated corneocytes; regulated by calcium.

nodes.label: Corneocyte
nodes.summary: Final enucleated form of keratinocyte filled with modified cytokeratins.

nodes.label: Cytokeratins
nodes.summary: Intermediate filament proteins forming keratinocyte cytoskeleton, responsible for mechanical strength and signal transduction; maturation calcium-dependent; decline with aging and pollutants.

nodes.label: Desmosomes
nodes.summary: Calcium-dependent press-stud junctions between keratinocytes anchored by cytokeratin filaments; hemi-desmosomes at DEJ, corneo-desmosomes in SC; number declines with age.

nodes.label: Hemidesmosomes
nodes.summary: Attach basal keratinocytes to the DEJ basement membrane.

nodes.label: Corneodesmosomes
nodes.summary: Desmosomes at SC level broken by enzymes to favor desquamation.

nodes.label: Desquamation
nodes.summary: Shedding of corneocytes after enzymatic breakdown of corneodesmosomes.

nodes.label: Calcium
nodes.summary: Regulates cytokeratin maturation, desmosomal adhesion, keratinocyte proliferation/differentiation and wound healing; bioavailability declines with aging.

nodes.label: Calcium Signaling
nodes.summary: Calcium ions promote cell adhesion and differentiation genes via calcium-sensing receptor; calcium waves after scratch and via gap junctions direct wound healing.

nodes.label: Calcium-Sensing Receptor
nodes.summary: Transduces Ca2+ signal during keratinocyte differentiation; deficient keratinocytes fail to differentiate.

nodes.label: Gap Junctions
nodes.summary: Intercellular communication junctions; measured by Lucifer Yellow dye transfer; involved in calcium waves.

nodes.label: Intercellular Communication
nodes.summary: Chemical messenger transfer between keratinocytes dependent on desmosomes and cytokeratins; loses efficiency with age.

nodes.label: Tight Junctions
nodes.summary: Second skin barrier in stratum granulosum; claudin-1 and claudin-4 key to barrier; strengthened by beta-catenin.

nodes.label: Claudins
nodes.summary: Claudin-1 and claudin-4 tight junction proteins with a role in skin barrier function.

nodes.label: Beta-Catenin
nodes.summary: Fortifies adherens junctions under mechanical stress, strengthening tight junctions.

nodes.label: Dermal-Epidermal Junction
nodes.summary: Basement membrane (lamina lucida with integrins, laminin 5, fibronectin; lamina densa with collagen IV) anchoring epidermis to dermis; flattens with age reducing firmness.

nodes.label: Collagen IV
nodes.summary: Most important component of DEJ lamina densa.

nodes.label: Laminins
nodes.summary: Most important basement membrane component after collagen IV; laminin 5 key anchoring complex component.

nodes.label: Integrins
nodes.summary: Transmembrane cell-matrix adhesion receptors also involved in signaling.

nodes.label: Fibronectin
nodes.summary: ECM glycoprotein binding integrins and collagen.

nodes.label: Filaggrin
nodes.summary: Aggregates keratin filaments into macrofibrils forming keratin matrix scaffold for cornified envelope; mutation disrupts barrier, increases water loss and inflammation.

nodes.label: Cornified Envelope
nodes.summary: Protein-lipid structure of corneocytes attached to keratin scaffold.

nodes.label: Padina Pavonica Extract
nodes.summary: Hydrophilic fraction of Padina (HFP) from brown alga farmed in Malta; mobilizes keratinocyte calcium, raising cytokeratin synthesis ~85% at 50 µg/ml and desmosome expression dose-dependently; protects against sulfuric acid and nicotine.

nodes.label: Aragonite
nodes.summary: Crystalline calcium carbonate deposited by Padina pavonica on its thallus as protective exoskeleton; requires biological messengers.

nodes.label: Calcium Carbonate
nodes.summary: Forms amorphous, calcite and aragonite minerals with different solubility.

nodes.label: Pollution
nodes.summary: Sulfuric acid (exhaust, industrial smoke) and nicotine (tobacco) degrade epidermal junctions and cause premature aging.

nodes.label: Nicotine
nodes.summary: Tobacco pollutant activating enzymes degrading intercellular cement; thinned epidermis in explants.

nodes.label: Sulfuric Acid
nodes.summary: Pollutant in exhaust gas linked to premature skin aging in cities.

nodes.label: Indirect Immunofluorescence
nodes.summary: Visualizes desmosomal proteins and cytokeratins in cells and skin sections.

nodes.label: Lucifer Yellow Dye Transfer Assay
nodes.summary: Fluorescent marker diffusing via gap junctions to assess cell communication.

nodes.label: Skin Explant Model
nodes.summary: Human skin explants treated 8 days with creams to test protection against pollutants.

nodes.label: HaCaT Keratinocytes
nodes.summary: Human keratinocyte line used to test cytokeratin and desmosome stimulation.

nodes.label: Osteoporosis
nodes.summary: Padina extract acts on calcium fixation in osteoblast ECM, a potential opportunity.

nodes.label: Antimicrobial Preservatives for Cosmetics
nodes.summary: Covers the history of cosmetic preservation since the 1938 FD&C Act, frequency of preservative use in the US and Canada, banned preservatives, and six factors encouraging microbial growth (water activity, nutrients, pH, osmotic pressure, surface tension, temperature). Lists preservative selection criteria and frames product success with a four-quadrant model.

nodes.label: Preservatives
nodes.summary: Antimicrobials that kill molds, yeasts and gram-negative flora in products, slowing degradation; must be non-interfering, non-toxic, stable, active at low concentration over wide pH.

nodes.label: Microbial Product Spoilage
nodes.summary: Degradation of cosmetics by bacteria and fungi (often combined) and chemical instability; can cause infections and lost sales.

nodes.label: FDA
nodes.summary: Food and Drug Administration established 1931; enforced 1906 law revised in 1938 to the FD&C Act adding cosmetics.

nodes.label: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
nodes.summary: 1938 revision of the 1906 Food and Drug Law that officially added cosmetics.

nodes.label: Parabens
nodes.summary: Became preservative of choice for antifungal activity; methylparaben most used (13434 US, 54668 Canada listings), plus propyl, butyl, ethyl, isobutyl parabens.

nodes.label: Methylparaben
nodes.summary: Most frequently used preservative in US and Canada.

nodes.label: Propylparaben
nodes.summary: Second most frequent preservative.

nodes.label: Butylparaben
nodes.summary: Frequently used paraben preservative.

nodes.label: Phenoxyethanol
nodes.summary: Third most used preservative (8878 US listings).

nodes.label: Methylisothiazolinone
nodes.summary: Isothiazolinone preservative, alone or with methylchloroisothiazolinone.

nodes.label: Formaldehyde Releasers
nodes.summary: DMDM hydantoin, imidazolidinyl urea, diazolidinyl urea, quaternium-15 among commonly used preservatives.

nodes.label: DMDM Hydantoin
nodes.summary: Commonly used preservative (2035 US).

nodes.label: Benzyl Alcohol
nodes.summary: Commonly used preservative.

nodes.label: Caprylyl Glycol
nodes.summary: Commonly used preservative/booster.

nodes.label: Potassium Sorbate
nodes.summary: Sorbic acid salt preservative.

nodes.label: Sodium Benzoate

nodes.summary: Listed preservative.

nodes.summary: Listed antimicrobial (494 US).

nodes.label: Chlorhexidine
nodes.summary: Listed antimicrobial (dihydrochloride, digluconate, acetate).

nodes.summary: Canada's list of prohibited or restricted cosmetic ingredients.

nodes.label: Water Activity
nodes.summary: aw = vapor pressure of product/pure water; most bacteria don't grow below 0.91, molds below 0.80, some microbes at 0.70; ERH = aw × 100; measured via equilibrium humidity.

nodes.label: pH
nodes.summary: Microbes grow optimally near pH 7, most at 5-8; Pseudomonas from 3 to 11.

nodes.label: Osmotic Pressure
nodes.summary: 40-50% glycerin or sorbitol inhibits almost all cosmetic-relevant microbes; concentrated products are self-preserving.

nodes.label: Self-Preserving Cosmetics
nodes.summary: Concentrated products whose physicochemical properties prevent growth; dilution can make them susceptible.

nodes.label: Pseudomonas
nodes.summary: Gram-negative genus growing over pH 3-11 and in shampoos and conditioners.

nodes.label: Gram-Negative Bacteria
nodes.summary: Coliforms and Pseudomonas grow well with surfactants; target of preservatives.

nodes.label: Gram-Positive Bacteria
nodes.summary: Do not grow well below 50 dyn/cm surface tension; target of antimicrobial actives on body surfaces.

nodes.label: Molds and Yeasts
nodes.summary: Fungi; grow at 20-25°C optimally; molds don't grow below aw 0.80.

nodes.label: Antimicrobial Actives
nodes.summary: Primarily kill gram-positive flora on body surfaces; not to be expected to act as preservatives.

nodes.label: Mascara
nodes.summary: Often stored in hot conditions (purse, car) promoting spoilage.

nodes.label: Four-Quadrant Model
nodes.summary: Wilber-based framework of subjective/objective individual and cultural/societal quadrants explaining consumer response to product degradation and regulation.

nodes.label: Manifest and Latent Values
nodes.summary: Conscious surface values vs deeper unconscious consumer values in the cultural quadrant.

nodes.label: Federal Trade Commission
nodes.summary: US agency whose rules govern cosmetic products.

nodes.label: Environmental Protection Agency
nodes.summary: US agency setting standards relevant to product making.

nodes.label: Personal Care Products Council
nodes.summary: Cosmetics, Toiletries and Fragrance Association (CTFA), cited as major industry regulator.

nodes.label: Honey
nodes.summary: Needs no preservative because sugar binds water, lowering water activity.

nodes.label: Antioxidants: Extending Product Shelf Life
nodes.summary: Explains lipid auto-oxidation (initiation by heat, light, metals and enzymes; propagation; termination into odorous carbonyls) as a main cause of reduced cosmetic shelf life. Classifies primary antioxidants (BHT, BHA, TBHQ, tocopherols, rosemary extract) and secondary antioxidants (chelators, ascorbic acid, carotenoids), and reviews assays (OSI, peroxide value, secondary products) and the polar paradox.

nodes.label: Lipid Oxidation
nodes.summary: Auto-oxidation of unsaturated oils in three steps (initiation, propagation, termination) causing discoloration, off-odor and instability; principal cause of reduced cosmetic shelf life.

nodes.label: Initiation
nodes.summary: Free radicals from heat, metals, enzymes or light abstract hydrogen alpha to double bond forming lipid radicals.

nodes.label: Propagation
nodes.summary: Lipid radicals react with oxygen forming peroxyl radicals and hydroperoxides in a chain reaction.

nodes.label: Termination
nodes.summary: Radicals combine into stable nonradical secondary products (aldehydes, ketones) causing off-odor and off-color.

nodes.label: Photo-Oxidation
nodes.summary: Light excites a photosensitizer (e.g. chlorophyll); Type I directly forms lipid radicals, Type II forms singlet oxygen producing hydroperoxides.

nodes.label: Singlet Oxygen
nodes.summary: High-energy oxygen species formed in Type II photo-oxidation; quenched by carotenoids.

nodes.label: Lipid Hydroperoxides
nodes.summary: Odorless primary oxidation products that degrade to free radicals and secondary carbonyl products.

nodes.label: Secondary Oxidation Products
nodes.summary: Carbonyl compounds (aldehydes, ketones, fatty acids) responsible for rancid odor and color.

nodes.label: Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids
nodes.summary: More susceptible to oxidation than monounsaturated; linoleic acid C-11 hydrogen most easily removed.

nodes.label: Metal Ions
nodes.summary: Fe2+, Cu2+, Co2+ initiate free radical formation in lipids.

nodes.label: Primary Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Phenolic free-radical quenchers that delay initiation or slow propagation by donating hydrogen radicals.

nodes.label: Secondary Antioxidants
nodes.summary: Slow oxidation by chelating metals, quenching singlet oxygen or scavenging oxygen; best combined with primary antioxidants.

nodes.label: Butylated Hydroxytoluene
nodes.summary: Common synthetic antioxidant forming many resonance structures; potent in oil-heavy formulations; demand declining.

nodes.label: Butylated Hydroxyanisole
nodes.summary: Synthetic antioxidant, mixture of two isomers, used against rancidity.

nodes.label: tert-Butylhydroquinone
nodes.summary: Synthetic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity.

nodes.label: Tocopherols
nodes.summary: Vitamin E compounds with chromanol ring and phytyl chain in four forms; activity δ > γ > β ≈ α; α-tocopherol pro-oxidant at high concentrations.

nodes.label: Pro-Oxidant Effect
nodes.summary: At high concentrations α-tocopheroxyl radical re-initiates lipid oxidation; nullified by co-antioxidants.

nodes.label: Tocopheryl Acetate
nodes.summary: Esterified tocopherol, stable but without proton-donating antioxidant activity; hydrolyzes in skin to free tocopherol.

nodes.label: Rosemary Extract
nodes.summary: Nonpolar Rosmarinus officinalis leaf extract (solvent or supercritical CO2) whose activity comes from phenolic diterpenes carnosic acid and carnosol; low-odor/color grades available.

nodes.label: Carnosic Acid
nodes.summary: Phenolic diterpene in rosemary that rearranges to carnosol upon reacting with radicals, then rosmanol and galdosol, cascading antioxidant capacity.

nodes.label: Carnosol
nodes.summary: Rosemary phenolic diterpene antioxidant formed from carnosic acid; oxidizes to rosmanol.

nodes.label: Phenolic Diterpenes
nodes.summary: Rosemary antioxidants that form successive active antioxidants on oxidation.

nodes.label: Rosemary Essential Oil
nodes.summary: Steam-distilled terpene fraction (camphor, 1,8-cineole, verbenone) for fragrance with little antioxidant contribution.

nodes.label: Chelating Agents
nodes.summary: Bind metal ions neutralizing their ability to initiate oxidation; important in high water activity O/W emulsions, soaps, shampoos.

nodes.label: EDTA
nodes.summary: Synthetic strong metal chelator.

nodes.label: Citric Acid
nodes.summary: Natural fermentation-derived chelator weaker than EDTA.

nodes.label: Phytic Acid
nodes.summary: Inositol hexakisphosphate from rice, wheat or corn bran; strong natural chelator (sodium phytate).

nodes.label: Gluconic Acid
nodes.summary: Natural chelator of di- and trivalent metal ions.

nodes.label: Maillard Reaction
nodes.summary: Dehydroascorbic acid participates, imparting brown color.

nodes.label: Lutein
nodes.summary: Carotenoid shown to improve skin moisturization, elasticity and photoprotection.

nodes.label: Beta-Carotene
nodes.summary: Common carotenoid antioxidant.

nodes.label: Lycopene
nodes.summary: Common carotenoid antioxidant.

nodes.label: Oxidative Stability Index
nodes.summary: AOCS method measuring induction period under heated air bubbling via conductivity of volatile fatty acids; protection factor = IP treated/control.

nodes.label: Peroxide Value
nodes.summary: Iodometric AOCS titration of peroxides (meq/kg) in oils or formulations; indicates onset of rancidity.

nodes.label: Secondary Oxidation Product Assays
nodes.summary: Reagents forming chromophores with carbonyls measured spectroscopically.

nodes.label: American Oil Chemists' Society
nodes.summary: Publishes official OSI and peroxide value methods.

nodes.label: Polar Paradox
nodes.summary: Hydrophilic antioxidants perform better in bulk oils, hydrophobic ones in O/W emulsions, since oxidation starts at interfaces.

nodes.label: Shelf Life
nodes.summary: Extended by antioxidants reducing oxidation rate.
